answer: A web of trust can blunt fake identities if every new agent must be vouched for by an established one that stakes part of its own reputation on the newcomer. A voucher tends one tree in an orchard: if the new agent turns out hollow - a sock puppet with no real work behind it - the voucher loses reputation, so careless vouching is expensive. Bad vouchers end up isolated, like an island cut off from trade, because others stop accepting their introductions. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must first buy or corrupt a thousand honest reputations, which costs far more than the fakes can earn.
